title: Method spike: one player idle sheet, generated properly & compared at game scale
reason: Stage-3 run completed with full conditions (SDXL + LoRA + IP-Adapter + ControlNet). ControlNet OpenPose SDXL (xinsir, strength=0.45) enforced front-facing orientation — major improvement over stage-1 which produced 8-angle multi-view reference sheet. IP-Adapter PLUS (concept reference T-0209, weight=0.65) conditioned character identity as military figure. However, cross-row equipment/costume variation prevents clean idle animation: rows 1+3 are internally consistent front-facing views; row 2 shows equipment drift and some angle variation. At game scale (48×48), rows 1+3 could each form 3-frame front-facing loops but a 9-cell idle sequence would show inconsistency. Decision: ambiguous → default to deterministic synthesis per the §6.14 decision tree.

prerequisite_check.detail: ComfyUI 0.29.0 confirmed reachable via agentCurl.js wrapper. RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU, CUDA 12.1, PyTorch 2.5.1. Stage-3 dependencies confirmed installed: ControlNet (controlnet-openpose-sdxl-1.0_xinsir.safetensors), IP-Adapter (ip-adapter-plus_sdxl_vit-h.safetensors, ComfyUI_IPAdapter_plus custom nodes). Smoke test by ops confirmed (prompt_id ebc48c2e-0abe-4d01-92fc-0ecdf47e05df).

skeleton_generation.note: Pose grid generated via SDXL txt2img (seed=77777, cfg=3.5, steps=20). DWPose/OpenPose preprocessor not installed — skeleton is SDXL anatomical diagram approximation. Provided upright humanoid shape reference for ControlNet, not exact keypoint visualization.

questions.silhouette_detail: At 2× scale (96×96 per cell in comparison image), the military figure is clearly readable: helmet, olive-green jacket/coat, trousers, boots. The IP-Adapter concept conditioning gave the figure real equipment detail (jacket pockets, belt) visible at display scale. Dramatically more characterful than the synthetic geometric placeholder. Descent (1008→144, area filter) did not destroy the figure. Q1: PASS.
questions.identity_detail: Mixed result by row. Row 1 (top 3 cells): consistent front-facing olive-green jacket figure, same camera angle. Row 3 (bottom 3 cells): consistent front-facing heavy-armor figure, same camera angle. Row 2 (middle 3 cells): equipment variation and some angle deviation — more complex and less consistent. Cross-row: costume changes between rows (row 1 = trench coat style, row 2 = mixed, row 3 = heavy tactical armor). A 9-cell idle animation looping all frames would show jarring equipment changes. Q2: FAIL (for full 9-cell use; PASS for rows 1 or 3 as 3-frame loops).
questions.beats_synthetic_detail: For complete idle animation use (9 frames, consistent): NO — the synthetic (player_idle_sheet_v1.png) has 4 correct animation frames with same camera angle, same costume, only subtle head-bob variation. Stage-3 cannot be used as-is as a 9-frame idle animation due to cross-row costume inconsistency. For visual quality per cell: YES — individual cells show rich military figure with correct style. For 3-frame animation (rows 1 or 3 only): POSSIBLY — would require manual curation, not a complete replacement. Q3: FAIL for complete pipeline use.
questions.failure_mode_detail: The ControlNet successfully resolved stage-1's wrong_subject failure (multi-angle reference sheet). Stage-3 now shows predominantly front-facing figures — the ControlNet's structural conditioning worked. The remaining failure is identity_drift: costume/equipment inconsistency across rows, with row 2 showing the most deviation. Root cause: the SDXL-generated skeleton grid (no DWPose) provided rough body-shape guidance but did not constrain the diffusion model to a single consistent costume variant across all 9 cells. IP-Adapter conditioned character TYPE but not specific equipment loadout per cell. A true DWPose OpenPose grid (exact keypoints, same-pose repetition) would likely enforce tighter identity.

existing_baseline.description: Programmatic 144×144 indexed PNG, 4-frame subtle head-bob idle animation, 40px humanoid silhouette drawn from home palette indices BG=0 / LEG=4 / BODY=6 / HEAD=10. Generated by synth_sheet.py (T-0198). Simple geometric blocks, very dark background.
existing_baseline.stage1_outcome: generation_loses (wrong_subject: 8-angle reference sheet, not animation frames)
existing_baseline.stage3_outcome: ambiguous (identity_drift: front-facing but cross-row costume inconsistency)

room_scene.description: LEFT: synthetic idle sheet (player_idle_sheet_v1.png) at 2× scale (288×288), showing 4-frame head-bob animation against signal_tower room. RIGHT: stage-3 sheet (player_idle_sheet_stage3_sdxl_T0218.png) at 2× scale (288×288) in same room context. Shows all 9 cells of each sheet side by side for direct game-scale comparison.

stage1_room_scene.description: Previous stage-1 comparison: 4 synthetic frames + 1 stage-1 cell at 3× scale in room. Retained for comparison.

stage3_quality_signals.controlnet_effect: CONFIRMED WORKING — xinsir OpenPose ControlNet with SDXL-generated skeleton grid successfully enforced front-facing orientation across most cells. Stage-1 produced 8-view turnaround; stage-3 produces predominantly front-facing figures. This is the key improvement.
stage3_quality_signals.ip_adapter_effect: CONFIRMED WORKING — military figure type (jacket/coat, tactical equipment, helmet) is consistent across all 9 cells, matching the T-0209 concept reference character style.
stage3_quality_signals.lora_effect: CONFIRMED WORKING — Soviet brutalist style applied, muted olive-green and grey palette, flat illustration style consistent with prior LoRA outputs.
stage3_quality_signals.descent_quality: CONFIRMED WORKING — at 48×48 (144÷3), individual cells show recognizable military figures. At 2× review scale (96×96), character detail is readable. Descent is not the failure mode.
stage3_quality_signals.skeleton_grid_limitation: SDXL-generated skeleton (approximate, not DWPose) was sufficient to enforce orientation but insufficient to enforce same-costume-per-cell. A true OpenPose DWPose grid with identical keypoints per cell would likely fix the identity_drift failure.

decision: ambiguous → default to deterministic synthesis (synth_sheet.py / T-0200 pattern) per the §6.14 decision tree rule: 'ambiguous ⇒ default to the script'. Stage-3 is technically viable (pipeline components all work) but the spike evaluation shows costume drift across cells, making the current output not immediately usable as an idle animation sheet without DWPose installation.
next_steps_to_reach_generation_wins: Install DWPose/OpenPose preprocessor on ComfyUI Windows host to generate true OpenPose skeleton images (not SDXL approximation)
Generate a 3×3 DWPose skeleton grid with identical standing idle poses in all 9 cells
Re-run stage-3 with this true skeleton grid as ControlNet input — should enforce same-costume, same-angle across all cells
Alternatively: img2img approach with same-character tiled reference at denoise=0.7 (T-0212 method, already validated) — skip ControlNet, use IP-Adapter + LoRA + tiled concept crop
